Chain: (1) [e_i,B]=[f_i,B]=0 at level 1 (Heisenberg commutes with U_q); (2) coefficientwise bar b is a ring automorphism of End(F) over Z and b(B)=P_e, so [bar e_i, P_e] = [bar f_i, P_e] = 0; (3) hence [e_i,P_e] = [e_i - bar e_i, P_e], and e_i - bar e_i is ENTRYWISE q^{-N} - q^{N} = -(q-q^{-1})[N]_q. Therefore [e_i,P_e] = (q-q^{-1})[E_i,P_e] with E_i integral. This is the structural reason the 2026-08-30 brief asked for; it does NOT restate C4. Slogan: B commutes with the Chevalley operators, so P_e commutes with their bar-conjugates, and the two differ by (q-q^{-1}) times an integral operator. Two-lemma proof: (i) an e-ribbon spanning r rows and c columns has r+c=e+1 (chain the row intervals: connected + no 2x2 forces b_{i+1}=a_i, then telescope); (ii) transposition is a bijection on ribbon additions exchanging r and c. Corollary (functional equation): Omega R_e(t) Omega = t^{e-1} R_e(1/t) for R_e(t)=sum_h t^h N^(h). Specialising t=-q and t=-q^{-1} gives the boxed identity Omega P_e Omega = (-q)^{e-1} B_{-1}^{[e]} and Omega B Omega = (-q^{-1})^{e-1} P_e. Since B = bar(P_e) coefficientwise, this IDENTIFIES THE BAR INVOLUTION WITH TRANSPOSITION on this operator. In the spin-centred normalisation Phat = (-q)^{-(e-1)/2} P_e the scalar disappears: the antilinear transposition Omega_bar fixes Phat (Hilbert-90 shape, c = bar(s)/s). LT 7.10 at k=1 then reads Omega_bar B Omega_bar = (-q)^{e-1} B, which is exactly our corollary. SETTLES Q56 (my linear Omega is NOT their involution; theirs is Omega_bar = b . Omega, and the passage between the two statements is B = bar(P_e)) and Q57 (yes -- Lemma r+c=e+1 IS the spin/cospin exchange for one ribbon, and (n-1)k = e-1 at k=1 matches on the nose).
